All six independently agree Phase VIII is a real, in-service (April 1, 2011) transmission expansion. Fuel=Gas and PipelineType=transmission both trivially correct -- every source calls it an interstate natural gas transmission pipeline/expansion.

validity.recommendation: orchestrator: check sibling FGT rows in this batch named 'Turkey Point Lateral', 'Manatee Lateral', 'Suwannee Lateral' (or an 'Arcadia to FPL Martin' lateral) for scope overlap with P4029's Phase VIII certificate -- likely NOT duplicates (see reasoning) but worth a positive confirmation rather than assuming
validity.researcher_notes: Reading FGT's original 2008 Phase VIII Notice of Intent (Federal Register E8-11695) to exhaustion turned up a scope wrinkle worth flagging even though it does not look like an actual duplicate. As ORIGINALLY proposed in 2008, Phase VIII was much bigger -- about 567.6 miles across 11 pipeline loops PLUS three greenfield lateral segments named 'Turkey Point Lateral' (6.7 mi, 24-in, Dade County FL), 'Manatee Lateral' (16.5 mi, 24-in, Manatee County FL), 'Suwannee Lateral' (22.0 mi, 20-in) and an 'Arcadia to FPL Martin Plant Lateral' (90.6 mi, 30-in) -- plus an outright acquisition of FPL's existing 20-in Martin Plant lateral. The task's roster of this batch's 17 FGT rows names exactly these segments among the OTHER 16 rows (Turkey Point Lateral / Alabama Power Lateral / Mobile Bay Lateral / etc.), so they clearly exist as separate GEM PIDs. But the AS-BUILT, in-service Phase VIII project that P4029 actually represents is only 483.2 miles (per the operator's own project page and EIA, both independent of the 2008 NOI) -- about 84 fewer miles than the 2008 proposal -- so at least some of those originally-proposed loops/laterals were evidently dropped, re-scoped, or deferred out of Phase VIII before it was finally certificated/built. I could NOT match any of them to a specific PID from the length/diameter columns in the 37-row roster given to me (none lines up cleanly with the 2008 proposal's preliminary specs, which is expected if the final built segment differs from the initial filing) -- so I am not asserting a specific duplicate PID, only flagging the scope history so whoever holds those sibling rows' shards can check their FERC docket numbers/build dates against CP09-17 and confirm they are NOT the same physical pipe P4029 already counts. This is a genuine finding from reading the source to exhaustion (rule 5), not a hunch.

Status='operating' confirmed: EIA's 2011 'Today in Energy' piece and the operator's project page (NRC-hosted mirror) both state the project was placed in service April 1, 2011 and has carried flows since; a 2021 PHMSA special-permit letter and 2023 PHMSA filings on FGT's letterhead ('An Energy Transfer/Kinder Morgan Affiliate') confirm the system is still an active, regulated, in-service pipeline a decade later. Independent origins: EIA (federal stats agency) vs. PHMSA filings vs. the operator's own historical page.

validity.recommendation: correct Owner1 -- the sheet lists the pipeline's own operating subsidiary as if it were its own owner; the actual legal owner is Citrus Corp (100% owner of Florida Gas Transmission Company, LLC per Citrus's own SEC-filed audited financials), whose stock is itself held 50/50 -- originally El Paso Corp / Southern Union Co (as of the SEC filing quoted), now Kinder Morgan Inc / Energy Transfer LP following the 2012 El Paso-Kinder Morgan and Southern Union-Energy Transfer mergers (confirmed by a 2021 PHMSA filing on FGT's letterhead, 'An Energy Transfer/Kinder Morgan Affiliate')
validity.researcher_notes: The sheet's Owner1='Florida Gas Transmission Co LLC' at 100% is backwards. Citrus Corp. and Subsidiaries' own SEC-filed audited financial statements (filed as Exhibit 99.2 to an Energy Transfer Partners 8-K, FY2011) state verbatim: 'Citrus Corp. (Citrus), a holding company formed in 1986, owns 100 percent of the membership interest in Florida Gas Transmission Company, LLC (Florida Gas)... At December 31, 2011, the stock of Citrus was owned 50 percent by El Paso Citrus Holdings, Inc.,... and 50 percent by CrossCountry Citrus, LLC,... an indirect subsidiary of Southern Union Company.' In other words: Citrus Corp owns FGT LLC, not the other way around, and Citrus itself is a 50/50 joint venture. A 2021 PHMSA special-permit letter, filed on FGT's own letterhead reading 'Florida Gas Transmission Company / An Energy Transfer/Kinder Morgan Affiliate,' independently confirms the modern-day 50/50 successor ownership (El Paso -> Kinder Morgan in 2012; Southern Union -> Energy Transfer in 2012). GEM's Owner field has 11 owner/percentage slots, which only makes sense if it is meant to capture the real equity chain -- as currently entered, the row states the pipeline owns itself, which is not informative and is technically incorrect. Two clearly independent origins: an SEC-filed, audited financial statement (Citrus Corp's own 10-K-style financials) vs. a PHMSA regulatory filing.
